Yes! You can generally bring a 20,000 mAh power bank on a flight in the United States, but it must go in your carry-on bag, not checked luggage. The key factor is its watt-hour (Wh) rating, not just its mAh capacity.

What are the rules?

According to the FAA's official battery travel guidance:

 Up to 100 Wh: Generally allowed in carry-on baggage without special approval.

101–160 Wh: Requires airline approval; up to two larger spare batteries are allowed per passenger.

 Checked luggage: Power banks are prohibited.

Packing: Protect the power bank from damage and prevent its terminals from short-circuiting.

Airlines may impose stricter restrictions, so check your carrier's rules before flying. FAA source.

Before you fly

Check the label on your power bank for its Wh rating. A typical 20,000 mAh bank rated at 3.7 V works out to about 74 Wh:

Pack it in your carry-on or personal item.

If your carry-on is gate-checked, remove the power bank and keep it with you in the cabin.

Bottom line: A typical 20,000 mAh power bank is allowed on US flights in carry-on baggage. Check the actual Wh rating and your airline's specific restrictions to be sure.
